# Code review iteration

Reviewed the whole `octomation/tuna` codebase at commit `0866134 2025-11-23`: all 52 Go files (`main.go`, `internal/{assistant,command,config,exec,llm,plan,response,tui,view}`), module files (`go.mod`, `tools/go.mod`), CI/CD workflows (`.github/workflows/*`), `.goreleaser.yml`, `.golangci.yml`, `Makefile`, `README.md`, and `CLAUDE.md`. Review angle: correctness, concurrency, security, API design, and how well the code and toolchain hold up against 2026-era Go idioms and CI practice. `.github/issues/` and `.github/roadmap/` were excluded as offline backlog dumps. No previous review files existed in `.github/reviews/` (the directory was created by this iteration), so all findings below are new.

Severity: **Crit** / **High** / **Med** / **Low** / **Nit**.
Class: `correctness` · `security` · `concurrency` · `perf` · `api` · `idiom` · `modern` · `test` · `build` · `docs`.

## 1. Detached executor goroutine races with the TUI lifecycle

Anchor: internal/command/exec.go:149-172, internal/tui/spinner.go:76-93, internal/command/plan.go:52-68.

```go
go func() {
    ctx := context.Background()
    summary, execErr = executor.Execute(ctx)
    program.Send(tuiexec.ExecutionDoneMsg{Err: execErr})
}()

if _, err := program.Run(); err != nil { ... }

if summary != nil && len(summary.Results) > 0 { ... }
return execErr
```

The executor runs in a goroutine whose only synchronization with the main goroutine is the `ExecutionDoneMsg` channel send. On the happy path that is fine, but `internal/tui/exec/model.go:125` lets the user quit with `q`/`ctrl+c` at any moment. When that happens `program.Run()` returns while the goroutine is still writing `summary` and `execErr` — a textbook data race (`go test -race` on this path would flag it). Worse, the executor is never cancelled: it keeps making paid API calls and writing files into `Output/` after the user has "quit", until `main` returns and the process dies mid-write.

The same pattern lives in `tui.RunWithSpinner` (internal/tui/spinner.go:79-93): `fn` runs inside `Init`'s `tea.Batch`, and `ctrl+c` quits the program with `m.err == nil`, so `RunWithSpinner` returns `nil` while `fn` still runs in the background. In `internal/command/plan.go:65` that means `result` is still `nil` when the code dereferences `result.PlanPath` — a nil-pointer panic (currently masked by the `safe.Do` recover in `main.go`, which converts it into a confusing "recovered" dump).

**Fix.** Tie the worker's lifetime to the TUI. Derive a `context.WithCancel` before `program.Run()`, cancel it when `Run` returns, and wait for the goroutine (`sync.WaitGroup` or a done channel) before touching `summary`/`execErr`. In the TUI model, treat `q`/`ctrl+c` as "cancel execution" rather than "abandon it". For `RunWithSpinner`, propagate a "user aborted" error and make callers treat a `nil` result as fatal instead of dereferencing it.

## 2. Failed tasks still produce a zero exit code

Anchor: internal/command/exec.go:194-222, internal/exec/executor.go:154-169.

`Executor.Execute` deliberately converts per-task failures into `summary.Errors` and returns `err == nil` (internal/exec/executor.go:154-169). But `executeNonInteractive` then prints the errors and returns `nil` unconditionally:

```go
if len(summary.Errors) > 0 {
    cmd.Println("\nErrors:")
    ...
}
return nil
```

A run where every single query fails (bad token, wrong model name, provider down) exits with code 0. Any script, Makefile, or CI job wrapping `tuna exec` will happily proceed with an empty `Output/` directory. The TUI path has the same flaw: `executeWithTUI` returns `execErr`, which is `nil` for task-level failures.

**Fix.** After execution, return a non-nil error when `len(summary.Errors) > 0`, e.g. `fmt.Errorf("%d of %d tasks failed", len(summary.Errors), total)` (wrap with `errors.Join(summary.Errors...)` for detail). If partial success should not be fatal, add an explicit `--allow-partial` escape hatch — but the default must be a failing exit code.

## 3. Goreleaser config still ships the go-tool template

Anchor: .goreleaser.yml:1-58.

```yaml
project_name: tool
...
brews:
  - name: tool
    caveats: An example of the goreleaser usage.
    description: Template for a typical CLI-tool written on Go.
...
release:
  github:
    owner: octomation
    name: go-tool
```

The release configuration was never adapted from the `octomation/go-tool` template. Tagging `v*` today triggers `.github/workflows/cd.yml`, which runs goreleaser and would: build a binary literally named `tool`, publish the GitHub release into the **octomation/go-tool repository** (not tuna), and push a Homebrew formula named `tool` with the description "Template for a typical CLI-tool written on Go". This is a release-pipeline defect that silently corrupts a sibling repository the moment the first tag is pushed.

**Fix.** Set `project_name: tuna`, `binary: tuna`, `release.github.name: tuna`, fix the brew formula name/description/homepage and its `bin.install`/completion lines, and dry-run with `goreleaser release --snapshot --clean` before the first real tag. While there, migrate to goreleaser v2 config (`version: 2`, `archives.formats`), since `version: latest` of the action will fetch a v2 goreleaser that rejects/deprecates parts of this v1 file.

## 4. CI references a missing workflow and pins Go versions the module cannot build with

Anchor: .github/workflows/ci.yml:104-110, .github/workflows/ci.yml:65-76, go.mod:3-5.

```yaml
release:
  name: Distribution
  needs: [ test ]
  uses: ./.github/workflows/cd.dist.yml   # file does not exist
```

`.github/workflows/` contains `cd.yml`, not `cd.dist.yml`, so on every `v*` tag the `release` job fails at workflow resolution. Independently, the test matrix pins `1.x / 1.20.x / 1.21.x` while `go.mod` declares `go 1.25.0` + `toolchain go1.25.5`. The `1.20.x` job is guaranteed dead — Go 1.20 predates automatic toolchain switching and hard-fails on a `go 1.25.0` requirement. The `1.21.x` jobs only work by silently downloading a different toolchain than the one advertised in the matrix, which defeats the purpose of a version matrix. The lint job pairs Go 1.21 with `golangci-lint-action@v3.7.0`, which pulls a modern golangci-lint that no longer accepts the v1 `.golangci.yml` (see [[#10. Toolchain, dependencies and CI actions lag years behind the module's Go 1.25 claim]]).

**Fix.** Point the `release` job at `./.github/workflows/cd.yml` (or delete the job, since `cd.yml` already has its own `push: tags` trigger and currently double-fires alongside ci.yml). Replace the matrix with `go-version-file: go.mod` plus at most one older supported version, and drop versions below the module's minimum.

## 5. Cobra command context and OS signals are never plumbed into execution

Anchor: internal/command/exec.go:153, internal/command/exec.go:194, main.go:30.

`main.go` carefully builds a context and runs `root.ExecuteContext(ctx)`, but the only long-running command in the tool ignores it: both `executeWithTUI` and `executeNonInteractive` create fresh `context.Background()` instead of using `cmd.Context()`. On top of that, `main.go` uses bare `context.WithCancel` with no signal wiring, so the context never cancels anyway. Consequences: in non-interactive mode SIGINT kills the process mid-file-write with no cleanup and no summary; there is no way to abort the rate-limiter wait (`router.go:97`); and a single hung HTTP request blocks the whole run forever because neither a request timeout nor an HTTP client timeout exists anywhere in `internal/llm`.

**Fix.** In `main`, use `signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)` (idiomatic since Go 1.16). In the exec command, use `ctx := cmd.Context()`. Add a per-request timeout (`context.WithTimeout` around `client.Chat`, configurable via `.tuna.toml`, e.g. default 120s) so one dead provider cannot wedge a whole plan.

## 6. Temperature zero is silently dropped by the OpenAI client

Anchor: internal/llm/client.go:77-85, internal/plan/plan.go:43.

```go
resp, err := c.client.CreateChatCompletion(ctx, api.ChatCompletionRequest{
    ...
    Temperature: float32(req.Temperature),
    MaxTokens:   req.MaxTokens,
})
```

`sashabaranov/go-openai` declares `Temperature float32` with `json:"temperature,omitempty"`. A user who runs `tuna plan --temperature 0` — the standard setting for reproducible prompt comparison, which is exactly this tool's purpose — gets the field omitted from the JSON body, and the provider applies its default (typically 1.0). The plan file says `temperature = 0.0`, the response metadata implies determinism, and the actual sampling was done at the provider default. For a prompt-comparison tool this quietly invalidates results. This is a long-documented go-openai footgun (their own docs suggest `math.SmallestNonzeroFloat32` as a workaround).

**Fix.** Either pass the documented sentinel (`float32(math.SmallestNonzeroFloat32)`) when the configured temperature is exactly 0, or better, migrate to a client whose request types use pointer/optional fields (the official `openai/openai-go` SDK, or build the request body manually). Also note `MaxTokens` is deprecated in favor of `max_completion_tokens` for current OpenAI models — worth handling in the same change.

## 7. Rating writes fail silently in the viewer

Anchor: internal/tui/view/model.go:384-388.

```go
resp.Rating = rating
// Save rating to YAML front matter in the response file
view.SaveRating(resp.FilePath, rating)
```

`view.SaveRating` returns an error (file deleted, permissions, disk full — it rewrites the whole response file via `os.WriteFile`), and the only call site discards it. The in-memory model is updated first, so the UI shows `[Good]`/`[Bad]` even when nothing was persisted; the user discovers the loss only on the next `tuna view`. Ratings are the primary artifact this screen produces, so silent loss defeats the feature. This would not survive the repo's own `errcheck` linter if the linter actually ran (see [[#4. CI references a missing workflow and pins Go versions the module cannot build with]]).

**Fix.** Capture the error and surface it in the TUI — set an `m.statusErr` field rendered in the footer, and only flip `resp.Rating` after a successful write. A `tea.Cmd` that performs the write and returns a `ratingSavedMsg{err}` is the idiomatic bubbletea shape.

## 8. Advertised exec flags parallel and continue are not implemented

Anchor: internal/command/exec.go:45-51, internal/command/exec.go:99-101, internal/exec/executor.go:44-49.

`tuna exec --help` advertises `--parallel, -p` ("Number of parallel requests") and `--continue` ("Continue from last checkpoint if interrupted"); README/CLAUDE.md repeat the promise. At runtime both degrade to a warning on stderr and sequential, restart-from-scratch behavior. `exec.Options.Parallel` and `Options.Continue` are threaded through `exec.New` into the executor and then never read (executor.go:122-192 is a plain nested loop). Shipping no-op flags is an API trap: users script `-p 8` in CI, never see the stderr warning, and conclude the tool is slow or billing is wrong. The dead `Options` fields also mislead future contributors into thinking the feature exists.

**Fix.** Either implement them (parallel is cheap now that the per-provider `rate.Limiter` exists: a `golang.org/x/sync/errgroup` with `SetLimit(parallel)` around `executeOne`, plus a mutex around `summary`; `--continue` can skip pairs whose `_response.md` already exists) or remove the flags and `Options` fields until they work. Hidden/experimental flags beat lying help text.

## 9. The core execution path has no test coverage while mock infrastructure sits unused

Anchor: internal/exec/executor_test.go:1-95, internal/deps_test.go:1-4, internal/llm/interface.go:6-9.

The `exec` package tests cover only `DryRun` string formatting and the two empty-input validation errors. `Execute`/`executeOne` — the code that reads query files, calls the LLM, accumulates tokens, emits progress events, and writes responses — has zero coverage, as does `llm.Client.Chat` and `llm.Router.Chat`'s rate-limit/alias/provider dispatch under error conditions. Ironically the codebase carries a full mocking apparatus for exactly this: the `ChatClient` interface exists explicitly to decouple the executor from HTTP, `golang/mock` is a direct dependency, and `internal/deps_test.go` imports `mockgen/model` "required for `make go-generate`" — yet not a single mock is generated or used. The riskiest behaviors found in this review (error accumulation semantics in [[#2. Failed tasks still produce a zero exit code]], progress-event ordering in [[#1. Detached executor goroutine races with the TUI lifecycle]]) are precisely the untested ones.

**Fix.** Add a hand-written fake `ChatClient` (5 lines; no codegen needed) and test `Execute` end-to-end against a `t.TempDir()` assistant layout: happy path, partial failure, context cancellation, and written-file content. Test `Client.Chat` against `httptest.Server` (go-openai honors custom `BaseURL`). Then delete the unused golang/mock plumbing (see [[#10. Toolchain, dependencies and CI actions lag years behind the module's Go 1.25 claim]]).

## 10. Toolchain, dependencies and CI actions lag years behind the module's Go 1.25 claim

Anchor: go.mod:3-23, tools/go.mod:1-21, .golangci.yml:1-17, .github/workflows/ci.yml:57-76.

The module declares `go 1.25.0`, but everything around it is frozen in 2022–2023:

- `github.com/pelletier/go-toml/v2 v2.0.0-beta.8` — a 2022 pre-release of the TOML parser that plans and configs depend on; current is v2.2.x with years of correctness fixes.
- `github.com/golang/mock v1.6.0` — archived by Google in 2023; maintained fork is `go.uber.org/mock`. Here it is also unused (see [[#9. The core execution path has no test coverage while mock infrastructure sits unused]]), so it can simply be dropped.
- `tools/go.mod` pins `golangci-lint v1.55.2` (Nov 2023, via personal forks in `replace` directives) and the archived `goreleaser/godownloader`; `.golangci.yml` is v1-format with `exportloopref` (removed — obsolete since Go 1.22 loopvar semantics and replaced by `copyloopvar`) and `gosimple`/`typecheck` (merged/not enableable in golangci-lint v2). A current linter refuses this config outright.
- CI pins `actions/setup-go@v5.0.0` with `go-version: 1.21.x`, `codecov/codecov-action@v3.1.4`, `golangci-lint-action@v3.7.0`, `goreleaser-action@v5.0.0` — all one or more majors behind, and the Go versions contradict go.mod (details in [[#4. CI references a missing workflow and pins Go versions the module cannot build with]]).
- `govulncheck` is wired into the Makefile (`check` target) but no CI job ever runs it, so vulnerability scanning is effectively opt-in local-only. Dependabot is configured (good) but its PRs clearly are not being merged.
- `github.com/sashabaranov/go-openai` is a community shim in maintenance mode; the official `openai/openai-go` SDK (v1+ since 2025) has typed optional fields that would also fix [[#6. Temperature zero is silently dropped by the OpenAI client]].
- `spf13/cobra v1.8.0`, `golang.org/x/net v0.33.0`, etc. — one to two years of patch releases behind.

**Fix.** One modernization pass: (1) `go get -u ./... && go mod tidy` on the main module; swap go-toml/v2 beta for v2.2.x and drop golang/mock. (2) Rebuild the tools story — delete `tools/` pins-via-forks; use `go.mod` `tool` directives (Go 1.24+) or install pinned tools in CI; adopt golangci-lint v2 with a `version: "2"` config and `copyloopvar`. (3) Refresh workflows: `go-version-file: go.mod`, current major of each action, add a `govulncheck` step, fix goreleaser (see [[#3. Goreleaser config still ships the go-tool template]]). (4) Start merging dependabot PRs or reduce its noise (grouped weekly updates) so it stays merged.

## 11. Byte-oriented string handling corrupts UTF-8 and ignores terminal width

Anchor: internal/tui/view/model.go:688-696, internal/tui/view/model.go:497-505, internal/tui/view/model.go:699-737, internal/command/view.go:98-121.

```go
func truncate(s string, max int) string {
    ...
    if len(s) <= max {
        return s
    }
    return s[:max-3] + "..."
}
```

`truncate`, `truncateLine`, `wrapText`, and the preview slicing in `printViewSummary` (`resp.Content[:50]`) all index by bytes. LLM output routinely contains em dashes, smart quotes, CJK, and emoji; slicing mid-rune yields broken `�` sequences in the TUI headers and previews, and byte length is the wrong metric for column layout anyway (a CJK rune is 3 bytes but 2 cells wide — `wrapText` will overflow the viewport it was written to protect). `printViewSummary` additionally removes newlines with a hand-rolled O(n²) scan-and-splice loop (internal/command/view.go:106-121) that is a one-liner in the standard library, and prints via `fmt.Printf` instead of `cmd.Printf`, bypassing the output streams the rest of the package respects. Minor same-era smells: `sort.Strings` instead of `slices.Sort` (internal/assistant/files.go:61) and a manual map copy instead of `maps.Clone` (internal/llm/router.go:155-161) in a module that requires Go 1.25.

**Fix.** Use `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi.Truncate`/`lipgloss.Width` (already in the dependency graph) or at minimum `[]rune`/`utf8`-aware helpers for every truncation; replace the newline scrub with `strings.NewReplacer("\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(preview)`; route output through `cmd`. Adopt `slices`/`maps` where the stdlib now covers it.

## 12. Query IDs from plan.toml reach the filesystem without validation

Anchor: internal/exec/executor.go:196-201, internal/exec/writer.go:45-48, internal/plan/loader.go:36-45.

`tuna exec` trusts `plan.toml` completely: each `query.ID` is joined into a read path (`filepath.Join(e.assistantDir, "Input", queryID)`) and a write path (`baseName + "_response.md"` under the model directory). A plan file containing `id = "../../../../home/user/.zshrc"` reads outside the assistant tree, and `id = "../../evil"` writes `_response.md` files outside `Output/`. Plans are normally tool-generated, but they are plain TOML in a directory users are encouraged to share/commit, and `tuna exec <id>` will happily execute a plan file that arrived via `git pull` from a teammate or an untrusted repo. `assistant.ValidateID` exists (internal/assistant/validate.go:19) but is only applied to `init`, not to plan consumption.

**Fix.** On plan load, validate every `query.ID` with the same rules as `ValidateID` (reject path separators, `..`, and absolute paths), or resolve the joined path and verify it stays under `assistantDir` (`filepath.Rel` + prefix check, or Go 1.24+ `os.Root`-scoped file access, which was built for exactly this).

## 13. Duration is persisted as raw nanoseconds despite a human-readable design

Anchor: internal/response/metadata.go:31-61, internal/response/metadata_test.go:158-181.

The whole point of the `metadataYAML` shim is a human-readable front matter — tokens are formatted as `100t` — but `Duration` is passed through as `time.Duration`, and `yaml.v3` has no encoder special-case for it (only the decoder parses strings like `2.45s`). Files written by `tuna exec` therefore contain `duration: 2450000000` while every test fixture and presumably every design doc shows `duration: 2.45s`. The tests never catch it because `TestFormat` only checks the round-trip, not the serialized text. Human-readable front matter is a stated feature of the response files (they are meant to be read and diffed in Markdown).

**Fix.** In `MarshalYAML`, emit `aux.Duration` as a string: change the field to `string` and set `aux.Duration = m.Duration.Round(10*time.Millisecond).String()`; the existing decoder path already parses it back. Add an assertion on the literal serialized output in `TestFormat`.

## 14. Small documentation and display inaccuracies

Anchor: internal/command/plan.go:29, internal/command/config.go:71, internal/llm/client.go:23-39.

Three small trust-eroding mismatches: (1) `tuna plan --help` says "Plan ID (UUID v4)" but IDs are ULIDs (`plan.go:73` uses `ulid.MustNew`); CLAUDE.md says ULID, so the help text is the outlier. (2) `tuna config show` prints `API Token:   $%s` from `p.APITokenEnv` — for providers configured with an inline `api_token` it renders a bare `$`, implying no token is set even though one is (config.go:71). (3) `llm.ConfigFromEnv` and the `llm.EnvAPIToken`/`EnvBaseURL` constants (client.go:12-39) are dead code — config loading moved to `internal/config` which duplicates the same constants — kept alive only by their own unit test.

**Fix.** Say "ULID" in the help text; in `config show`, print `$ENV_NAME` when `APITokenEnv` is set and `(inline, hidden)` when `APIToken` is set; delete `ConfigFromEnv` and the duplicated constants together with their test.
